newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank says cancels liquidity bill auction.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank says cancels liquidity bill auction.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Monday said it had cancelled this week's liquidity bill auction, the third consecutive week it has done so.

"We are not issuing our bills because instead we are considering possible intervention via sales of Finance Ministry T-bills to maturity date from our portfolio," Peter Andresic, NBS chief dealer, told Reuters.
"It is one alternative which we have chosen now that the ministry has switched to longer-term treasury issues," Andresic added.
The NBS bought some 1.85 billion crowns worth of four-week T-bills for its own portfolio in the past two auctions, and a part of them has already been sold, Andresic said.

Earlier on Monday, the ministry has announced an auction of nine-month T-bills for Wednesday, the first of such a maturity this year. The ministry said was issuing longer maturity bills to help cover the expected 1996 budget deficit.
"However, the NBS cannot buy T-bills longer than three- months according to law," Andresic added.
